summary: 1. Jump immediately into the action or question within the first 3 words instead of using warm-up fluff like 'You've used soap your whole life'. 2. High-stayed hooks (up to 42.9% stayed) ask direct, visually descriptive questions ('Why does baking soda fizz the moment it hits vinegar?') rather than abstract setups. 3. Video titles that state a direct, relatable curiosity question perform better on retention than titles padded with textbook jargon like ': Chemistry Explained'. 4. Keep videos focused under 40 seconds, as the 57-second video had the lowest views (16 views) despite decent retention. 5. Avoid long wordy setups with complex scenarios (e.g., comparing 10kg vs 1kg spheres in a vacuum) which stall audience momentum immediately.
winning_hooks: Direct action-focused questions starting immediately with 'Why' or immediate phenomenon ('Why does baking soda fizz the moment it hits vinegar?')
avoid: Preamble statements before the question ('You've used...', 'You've seen...')
Academic subtitle titles like ': The Chemistry of Cleaning' or ': Chemistry Explained'
Complex, multi-sentence hypothetical setups in the first 5 seconds
next_experiment: Test a direct question hook starting at second 0 ('Why does X do Y?') against a preamble hook ('You see X every day, but why does Y happen?') using identical visual B-roll and script length (~35s).
